headline: The heads of Japan's Nomura and Daiwa securities groups expect the stock rally to last, but warn that a turn against AI could end it.
score_reason: On-record forecasts and warnings from two securities chiefs; pool score 6 kept.
importance_line: It matters most to Japanese investors, since a turn against AI is the main threat the two chiefs name, but these are their own forecasts, and the Nikkei closed Thursday at 69,042.11, short of the 75,000 to 80,000 they expect by year-end.
summary: The Japan Times reports that Nomura Holdings chief executive Kentaro Okuda and Daiwa Securities Group chief executive Akihiko Ogino expect Japan's stock rally to extend well into 2027. Both warned that a change in investor mood toward AI could reverse the rally, with Okuda calling that a "significant risk" and Ogino saying views can change "dramatically over a very short period of time."
notes: Read in full from the Japan Times. Both executives spoke at a Nikkei event in Tokyo on Thursday 8 Oct 2026; the Nikkei 225 is Japan's main stock index.
